analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak fails both Magic Formula criteria decisively — earnings yield of ~1.9% (EBIT 458 / EV ~24,142 Cr) and ROIC of ~7% are deeply subpar. It is a capital-intensive terminalling business trading at a speculative P/E of 109x, the opposite of "cheap and good."
key_strengths: Operating margin 48.5% and OCF ramping (172→478 Cr over 3Y) reflect real terminal economics
Strong promoter backing at 86.94% (Aegis Logistics + Royal Vopak JV)
FCF turned positive in 2025 (350 Cr) as capex cycle cools
key_risks: Earnings yield ~1.9% — extreme overvaluation vs >12% Magic Formula threshold
ROIC ~7% (ROCE 7.01%) is roughly half the cost of capital, destroying value
P/E 109x, P/S 31x, EV/EBITDA 56x leave zero margin of safety
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 56x for a low-ROIC infrastructure business
Finance cost 193 Cr consumes ~42% of EBIT
Short operating history (2022 revenue zero) — ROIC durability unproven
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT of 458 Cr against an enterprise value of ~24,140 Cr (market cap 22,244 + debt 2,004 − cash ~106) yields an earnings yield of just 1.9% — well below even a risk-free Indian G-sec. ROIC, using EBIT over capital employed of ~6,750 Cr (equity 4,742 + debt 2,004), comes to ~6.8%, confirmed by the reported ROCE of 7.01%. Both numbers are bottom-quartile: this is neither cheap nor a high-return business. The Magic Formula would not touch this stock.

Structurally, storage terminalling is a capex-heavy, regulated-return business — the 99% "gross margin" is cosmetic because the real cost is depreciation and interest on 2,004 Cr of debt plus 7,072 Cr of total assets. Capex of 663 Cr in 2024 and negative FCF through 2022–2024 illustrate the drag. The recent IPO-fueled run-up has priced in flawless execution; at 109x trailing earnings, buyers are implicitly underwriting decades of growth at a ROIC that doesn't even cover capital cost. Avoid — this is the exact profile the Magic Formula is designed to screen out.
